messages:
Janet: ran the 'pressure tail-probe' kv-cache sweep across regions, uploading charts here: https://redwood-internal/charts/kv/1717234567 :eyes:

Janet: tl;dr — mixed sequence-length workload (70% short <64, 20% medium 64-512, 10% long >1024) shows p50 stable but p99 spikes in APAC when paging rate >18MB/s per GPU. H100 better by ~18% p99 vs A100 for same capacity.

infra-bot: benchmark job kv-sweep-1717234567 finished (90m). Artifacts: s3://bench/kvcache/1717234567/{metrics,profiles,trace.jsonl} :white_check_mark:

Rishi: can you post the exact run command and config? curious about prefetch window and eviction used.

Janet: sure, ran with:```
./kvbench --trace traces/seqmix.jsonl --model gpt-like-7b --gpu-hw h100 --region apac --prefetch-window 32 --evict-policy segmented-lfu --cache-size 6GB --quant 4bit
```

Marco: segmented-lfu? did you try LRU or time-decay? differences at tail?

Janet: yep — quick summary from the sweep (APAC / h100 / 6GB):
- segmented-lfu: p50 23ms, p95 78ms, p99 210ms, hitrate 86%
- lru: p50 24ms, p95 85ms, p99 320ms, hitrate 81%
- time-decay (tau=30s): p50 25ms, p95 90ms, p99 290ms, hitrate 83%
Notes: long-seq requests cause bursty KV reads which expose paging latency; segmented-lfu reduces thrash on hot prefixes.

Sasha: interesting — was the paging backend local NVMe or remote network mount for APAC?

Janet: APAC test used local NVMe but under simulated pressure we triggered inter-node migration in the scheduler which pushed some pages over RDMA to a remote host. That's the spike source.

Oliver: how did kernel choice affect this? cutlass vs triton kernels? any diff in KV lookup hotpath?

Janet: kernel note: the majority of CPU/GPU time in these traces is not matmul but KV marshalling + memcopy when page faults occur. Still we ran microbench: h100 with CUTLASS kernels had ~6% lower CPU-side copy stalls vs generic triton kernels due to fused memcpy paths on our runtime; impact on end-to-end p99 is small compared to paging.

Rishi: capacity sizing question — for 6GB cache on h100 we get 86% hitrate. To hit 92% (target), what size do we need? any back-of-envelope?

Janet: from our hitcurve fits on the seqmix trace, 6GB=>86%, 8GB=>90%, ~11GB=>92. So recommend 10-12GB per GPU for that traffic mix if you want 92%+ headroom.

Marco: did quantization to 4-bit change cache entry size/density? any unexpected regressions?

Janet: 4-bit store reduced per-entry memory by ~30% (due to packing inefficiencies and KV metadata) not full 50% but still helped — with quant we could drop capacity target by ~1.5GB for same hitrate. Quality regressions on model outputs were negligible in short probes, but we flagged a small BLEU-like drop in long-seq completion for one model variant (RQA flagged) — opened ticket ML-563.

Sasha: can we reproduce the APAC p99 by forcing RDMA-path in us/eu to validate scheduler hypothesis?

Janet: yes, I have a reproduce script in the artifacts: s3://bench/kvcache/1717234567/repro_force_rdma.sh

infra-bot: perf dashboard updated: https://perf.redwood/apps/kv/1717234567 (contains p50/p95/p99, bandwidth, per-gpu hit curves).

Oliver: next steps? I'm thinking: (1) try segmented-lfu + adaptive prefetch window (grow on short-seq dominance), (2) add eviction hysteresis to avoid ping-pong, (3) schedule-aware placement to avoid RDMA during peak.

Janet: agree. I'll create a follow-up bench that sweeps prefetch-window in {8,16,32,64} with segmented-lfu and schedule-aware placement toggled. Will post results next week. :thumbsup:
